patients.summary: Construction laborer with advanced HIV who has declined antiretroviral therapy since a brief course in 2016, asplenic after a 2011 crash, on TMP-SMX prophylaxis he takes unevenly. Develops HIV-associated mixed cryoglobulinemia with neuropathy and renal involvement in 2023, then pulmonary and cutaneous nocardiosis in May 2026 and CNS nocardiosis with an ICU stay in July 2026, when ART is finally started.

documents.title: New Patient Call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to establish primary care with us. Says his last clinic "wasn't working out" and he hasn't had a regular doctor in a while. Medicaid, verified active. Mentions he has HIV and takes an antibiotic a few times a week. New patient slot given for Mon 9/20 at 8:40. Release of records form emailed so we can get his old chart. He works construction days, prefers early appointments.

documents.title: Records from Prior Clinic
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Faxed records, 38 pages, from the community health clinic he used before. Summary for the PCP:
- HIV-1 infection diagnosed 2016 at that clinic. Started on an antiretroviral regimen at diagnosis, notes say he stopped it on his own within the first year; repeated counseling documented, he declined restarting.
- CD4 below 200 on their last several draws; viral load in the tens of thousands.
- On TMP-SMX DS three times weekly for PCP prophylaxis.
- Anemia attributed to chronic disease; mild CKD on their problem list.
- MVC around 2011: both femurs fixed, spleen removed, several transfusions. Right knee arthritis since.
- Hepatitis A and hepatitis B vaccine series documented as complete.
- NKDA.
Records placed in chart for review at the 9/20 visit.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

45 y/o man here to set up primary care. Old clinic records reviewed (arrived 9/14).

HIV: diagnosed 2016. Took ART for a few months back then, didn't like how it made him feel and stopped; hasn't been on anything since. Knows his counts are low. Takes Bactrim DS M/W/F "most weeks" - honest that he forgets some. No current fevers, sweats, cough, thrush, diarrhea or skin problems.
Other: anemia (told it's from the HIV), mild kidney disease on old list, right knee arthritis after the 2011 crash - uses ibuprofen 400 or Tylenol 500 when the knee acts up on the job.

PSH: 2011 MVC - ORIF both femurs, splenectomy, multiple transfusions. 
Meds: TMP-SMX DS 1 tab three times weekly; ibuprofen 400 q6h prn; acetaminophen 500 q6h prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father - HTN, CAD. Mother - type 2 DM, hypothyroid. No immunodeficiency, autoimmune or bleeding disorders in the family.
SH: laborer for a construction outfit, lives alone in Amherst. Quit cigarettes about 8 yrs ago. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a month. 

Exam: well-appearing, thin. No oral thrush or lesions. No lymphadenopathy. Lungs clear. RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, healed midline scar, no organomegaly. Old scars both thighs. R knee with crepitus, no effusion, full extension. Skin without rash. Feet: normal sensation.

A/P
1. HIV, advanced, off ART. Long talk. Explained that modern once-daily regimens are much easier than what he took in 2016 and that being off treatment with low CD4 is the biggest risk to his health. He's not ready - wants to "think about it." Offered HIV clinic referral, declined for now. Will check CD4/VL today and keep raising it.
2. PCP prophylaxis - continue TMP-SMX DS three times weekly; set phone alarm.
3. Asplenia + HIV - needs pneumococcal, meningococcal ACWY and B, Hib. Nurse visit in Oct with flu shot.
4. Anemia of chronic disease - CBC.
5. CKD 2 - CMP, UA, urine albumin.
6. R knee post-traumatic arthritis - ibuprofen/APAP prn as before.
7. Hep C screen today. Hep A/B vaccination documented in old records.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Todd - your labs are back. Your CD4 count is low and the virus is very active in your blood, which is what we expected off treatment. Your blood count shows the same mild anemia as before, kidney function is about where your old records had it, and hepatitis C screen is negative. Cholesterol is fine. My offer stands on getting you back on HIV medicine whenever you're ready - one pill a day these days. Please keep taking the Bactrim. See you in October for shots.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP plan for asplenia/HIV. Afebrile. Given: flu (L deltoid), PCV20 (R deltoid), MenACWY dose 1 (L deltoid), Hib (R deltoid). VIS sheets given. Tolerated, waited 15 min without issue. Next: MenACWY #2 and MenB #1 in about 8 weeks - booked 11/16.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: MenACWY #2 and MenB #1 given. Also asked for his COVID booster - primary series was at a pharmacy this spring per his card, booster given today. Sore arm from last round lasted a day. MenB #2 due in a month, booked 12/14.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: MA
documents.body: MenB dose 2 given L deltoid. Series complete. Asplenia vaccines now done except MenACWY booster in 5 yrs - added to health maintenance.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing OK. Working through the cold weather, knee stiff in the mornings, ibuprofen a couple times a week helps. Taking Bactrim "better than before." Still not ready for HIV meds - says he'll think about it after the winter.
O: Vitals reviewed. Thin, no thrush. Lungs clear. R knee crepitus, no effusion. Skin clear.
A/P: HIV off ART - re-offered, declined, door left open. Prophylaxis continues. Knee - prn analgesics. Turning 46 this week: FIT kit given for colon cancer screening. RTC May with labs.

documents.title: FIT Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Repeat yearly. Letter to patient.

documents.title: TMP-SMX Refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Electronic request from his pharmacy, TMP-SMX DS #36 (three times weekly). Last fill 12/2021 - a bit later than expected for a 12-week supply. Approved x1 with 3 refills per standing plan. Flagged for PCP re: adherence.

documents.title: HIV Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subjective: no fevers, night sweats, cough, mouth sores, diarrhea, rashes. Working full days, busy season. Admits to missing "a few" Bactrim doses a month. Knee fine lately.
Objective: vitals stable, weight steady. No thrush, no nodes. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Skin clear.
Assessment/Plan:
- Advanced HIV off ART: we talked again about starting a single-tablet regimen; he says his old meds made him sick and he's afraid of that again. Explained side effects are far less common now. Still declines; would rather not see an HIV clinic. Respecting that, will keep offering.
- PCP prophylaxis: pill box given.
- Anemia, CKD 2: CBC, BMP today.
- CD4/VL today.
Follow up at physical in fall.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Todd, labs are about the same as September: CD4 still low, viral load still high, mild anemia unchanged, kidney numbers stable. Nothing new, but the CD4 is the one I worry about. Keep up the Bactrim and let me know any time you want to talk about treatment.

documents.title: RE: Lab Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: thanks doc. got it. still thinking

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL EXAM - 46M

Interval: no illnesses this year. No ED visits. Still off ART by choice. Bactrim most days it's due.
ROS negative: no weight loss, fevers, sweats, cough, dysphagia, diarrhea, rash, urinary symptoms, numbness.
Meds: TMP-SMX DS three times weekly, ibuprofen 400 prn, APAP 500 prn. NKDA.
Social: same job, lives alone. Former smoker. Rare alcohol.

Exam: NAD. HEENT: no thrush, dentition fair. Neck: no nodes, no thyromegaly. Lungs clear. CV: RRR, no murmur. Abd: soft, nontender, scars healed. Ext: no edema, R knee crepitus. Skin: no rash or lesions. Neuro: sensation intact feet, reflexes symmetric.

Plan:
- Health maintenance: flu, bivalent COVID and Tdap today. FIT kit for this winter. Asplenia series complete.
- HIV: labs. ART discussion again - "maybe next year."
- Kidneys/anemia: CMP, CBC, UA, urine albumin.
- PHQ-2 negative.
RTC 4-5 months.

documents.title: Refill Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called, out of Bactrim for about a week - pharmacy said no refills left. Sent 12-week supply per protocol. Reinforced three times weekly dosing; he says job site hours made him lose track. Suggested keeping the bottle in his truck. FIT kit still at home - reminded.
